description: A shared Renovate preset. Extend it from another repository with
It carries the POLICY from Fleetwright's own renovate.json and none of the
facts about that one project: no package names, no paths, no managers that
read a file only Fleetwright has. Four rules.
PIN EVERYTHING; NO RANGES. rangeStrategy: pin, so a manifest names an exact
version and every change to what runs is a diff somebody can read. A caret
hides the update inside the lock file.
LET A RELEASE SOAK. minimumReleaseAge holds an update back for three days
before it is proposed. Not for stability, which CI answers in minutes, but
for the supply chain: a malicious version is usually found and pulled within
hours to a couple of days, and three days is somebody else finding it first.
A SECURITY FIX STILL DOES NOT WAIT. vulnerabilityAlerts overrides the soak to
nothing, because there the known-bad version is the one already installed.
STAY ON LATEST OTHERWISE. Majors are proposed like anything else; holding
them for review buys safety CI already provides and pays for it in a
backlog. GitHub Actions patch and minor updates are grouped and automerged,
because every workflow run covers them and a break is one click to revert.

vulnerabilityAlerts.description: A security fix does not wait for anything, the soak included: the known-bad version is the one already installed.

packageRules.description: Actions are grouped and automerged on patch/minor: every workflow run covers them, so a break is visible immediately and revertible in one click.
package.json's engines floor is a compatibility claim about what the code needs, not a statement about what CI runs. Renovate moves the runner; a person moves the claim.

customManagers.description: The Node every workflow sets up, `node-version:` under actions/setup-node. The github-actions manager reads `uses:` and not an action's inputs, so an exact version written there would otherwise never move. Exact versions only: a bare major in a matrix is a person's choice of which lines to test.
